MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS
Sustainable Growth
Sustainability remains integrated into our operational 
and strategic decision-making, supporting long-term 
efficiency and resilience. Investments in renewable 
energy, equipment electrification, waste-to-energy 
systems, water recycling and resource optimisation 
initiatives are helping reduce environmental impact 
while strengthening operational performance and 
responsible growth.
Operational Overview
FY 2025-26 marked a transformational year for our 
Company, driven by significant scale-up across mining, 
pellet and DRI operations, alongside continued 
progress in downstream integration and strategic 
diversification. Total income for the year stood at ₹ 
1,38,378 Mn, registering a robust year-on-year growth 
of 104%, while EBITDA increased by 133% to ₹ 46,731 
Mn. EBITDA margins expanded to 33.77%, reflecting 
improved operating leverage, a richer product mix and 
stronger operational efficiencies. Growth during the 
year was supported by higher iron ore environmental 
clearance limits, rapid ramp-up of the pellet plant, 
improved sponge iron volumes and strong domestic 
demand for iron ore and pellets. The commissioning 
of the slurry pipeline further strengthened evacuation 
efficiency, throughput and overall asset utilisation 
across operations.
Our Company incurred capital expenditure of ₹ 81,310 
Mn during FY 2025-26 as part of our ongoing expansion 
and integration strategy. Iron ore production for the 
year stood at 21.96 MnT, while sales volumes reached 
16.18 MnT, supported by a strong monthly run-rate of 
approximately 2 MnT. In the DRI segment, sales volumes 
increased to 479.69 KT, supported by stable realisations 
and improved operational performance. FY 2025-26 also 
marked the successful ramp-up of the pellet business 
with pellet production reaching 3.03 MnT following 
commercial production commencing towards the 
end of Q2 FY 2025-26. The pellet plant achieved 100% 
capacity utilisation within four months of commissioning, 
supported by strong product quality, captive ore 
availability and the slurry pipeline network, contributing 
to robust realisations and margins.
During the year, our Company also strengthened its 
strategic diversification into critical minerals through 
international acquisitions in the Democratic Republic 
of Congo. We acquired a 50% stake in the operational 
Surya Mines platform and a 49% stake in the Chemaf 
Group, establishing an integrated copper–cobalt 
platform supported by high-grade resources, established 
infrastructure and long-term scale-up potential. Together, 
these platforms provide a pathway towards approximately 
100,000 TPA copper capacity and around 20,000 TPA 
cobalt capacity, positioning our Company to participate in 
the growing global demand for critical minerals linked to 
electrification and energy transition trends.

MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS
Business Outlook
Our Company enters the medium and long term with a 
degree of clarity and operational confidence uncommon 
for a business of its age and scale. Foundational 
investments in beneficiation, pellets, integrated 
steelmaking, logistics infrastructure and global mineral 
diversification represent a deliberate and irreversible 
repositioning from a merchant iron ore miner into a fully 
integrated, low-cost metals producer with a diversified 
and increasingly resilient earnings base. Our captive 
resource base supported by a mining lease valid through 
2057 and a reserve profile spanning both direct-shipping 
and beneficiation-grade ore, ensures access to raw 
materials at structurally advantaged costs across every 
phase of this journey.
As downstream assets are progressively commissioned 
and the value chain deepens, an increasing share of the 
value embedded in each tonne of iron ore extracted will 
be captured. This margin curve progression is supported 
by our own infrastructure, power and logistics, rather 
than by market conditions alone. The Mine Development 
and Operations business further adds a layer of earnings 
predictability, reducing the overall cyclicality of the 
portfolio. In parallel, our Company’s entry into copper 
and other critical minerals positions us to participate in 
the global energy transition as a resource provider rather 
than merely as an observer. Conscious of the execution 
demands this ambition places on its people, systems 
and capital discipline, our Company remains committed 
to delivering our programme in a manner that creates 
enduring value for all stakeholders such as shareholders, 
employees, communities and the nation it serves.
Risk Management
Our Company has established a robust Risk 
Management Framework that enables the timely and 
effective identification, assessment and mitigation 
of key business risks. This framework plays a critical 
role in supporting the achievement of our Company’s 
corporate objectives.
Risk and Concerns
The key risks faced by our Company include global 
steel demand dynamics, economic slowdown, market 
volatility, rising finance costs and potential constraints 
or significant increases in raw material prices. While no 
material long-term risks are anticipated, the following 
specific challenges have been identified:
	
↘Our Company’s operations, ongoing projects and 
profitability may be impacted by delays in approvals 
and procedural processes, as well as any unfavourable 
changes in government policies relating to mining, 
allocations and tariffs.
	
↘The mining and steel industries operate under 
stringent labour laws and health and safety 
regulations. Any lapse in safety could lead to 
damage to property, assets and human capital. In 
addition, labour shortages may adversely impact our 
Company’s operations and ongoing projects.
	
↘Rising environmental concerns and regulatory 
requirements relating to carbon emissions 
and water availability may impose operational 
constraints, potentially impacting our Company’s 
growth trajectory.
	
↘Operating in a socio-economically sensitive region, any 
unrest could adversely affect mining operations.
Risk Mitigation and Management
Our Company has clearly defined the roles and 
responsibilities of the Board of Directors and the 
Risk Management Committee in overseeing and 
administering our risk management procedures. 
These responsibilities ensure that corrective actions are 
implemented promptly and consistently when required. 
The Board identifies and categorises risks across 
key areas, including operations, finance, marketing, 
regulatory compliance and corporate affairs.
Our Company undertakes biannual reviews of “List of 
Risk Areas” to identify emerging risks and implement 
appropriate mitigation measures. We also obtain 
compliance confirmations from relevant units and 
divisions on statutory requirements. The Internal Auditor 
assesses risk levels during audits and reports findings 
to the Audit Committee. Overall, our Company’s risk 
management framework is robust and comprehensive, 
safeguarding operations while ensuring preparedness for 
potential contingencies.
Internal Control Systems 
We adopt a structured approach and prioritises the 
implementation of effective checks to ensure operational 
efficiency and accuracy. We maintain an appropriate and 
comprehensive system of internal controls that align with 
our size and the nature of our operations. Our Company’s 
internal control system provides reasonable assurance for 
safeguarding assets and ensuring proper authorisation, 
recording and reporting of transactions.
Our Company’s internal auditors conduct audits across 
various departments and areas. We report the findings 
and observations from the Internal Audit Department to 
the Audit Committee, which meets regularly to review 
the audit issues and oversees the implementation of 
corrective actions. Additionally, the statutory auditors 
provide assurance regarding the adequacy of our 
Company’s internal control systems. Overall, these strong 
auditing and oversight mechanisms help ensure that 
our Company’s internal controls remain effective and 
aligned with best practices, promoting transparency and 
accountability within our operations.
Human Resources and  
Industrial Relations 
Our Company’s Human Resources Department (HRD) is 
committed to fostering a safe, collaborative and positive 
work environment that promotes strong relationships 
between workers and staff. We firmly believe that 
employees at all levels are integral to achieving 
organisational objectives. Our Company encourages 
a culture of continuous improvement and adaptability 
through regular training programmes that enhance 
skills, knowledge and productivity while keeping 
employees updated on the latest practices. Senior 
management remains accessible to provide guidance 
and address grievances effectively. The HRD consistently 
works to strengthen harmony and coordination across 
the organisation, while prioritising employee safety 
through strict adherence to safe working practices. As of 
March 31, 2026,  our Company had 4,866  employees, 
with industrial relations remaining peaceful and cordial 
throughout the year.

Value Added Products
Sponge Iron Division
The Sponge Iron Division delivered record production 
in FY 2025-26, benefiting from the commissioning of 
the new 360 KTPA DRI plant at Ghugus in Q2 FY 2025-
26. Combined with the modernised existing facilities 
at Ghugus and the DRI plant at Konsari, the Division 
achieved its highest-ever output.
PERFORMANCE HIGHLIGHTS FOR THE 
YEAR AND OUTLOOK
Review of Operations
The Company during the year had 02 (Two) separate 
business segments – Mining, Value added Products 
("VAP"). The Segment-wise performances are as below:
Mining
The Iron ore mining activities continued its operating 
excellence at Surjagarh area of Gadchiroli district of the 
State of Maharashtra.
FY 2025-26 was a landmark year for the Mining 
Division. The Company achieved its highest-ever 
iron ore production of 21.96 Million Tonnes ("MnT"), 
The above production showed an increase of 57% as 
compared to the previous FY. DRI sales volume for 
FY 2025-26 stood at 479,690 MT (56% Y-o-Y increase), 
with a realisation of ₹27,009 per tonne and EBITDA per 
tonne of ₹6,643.
Power Division
The Power Division continued to operate smoothly, 
meeting the in-house power requirements of the 
Sponge Iron and Pellet manufacturing operations at 
representing a 120% year-on-year increase over 10 MnT 
in FY 2024-25. This exceptional performance was driven 
by the enhancement of the Environmental Clearance 
("EC") limit from 10 Million Tonnes Per Annum ("MTPA") 
to 55 MTPA, the commissioning and utilisation of the 
85 km slurry pipeline (Hedri to Konsari), optimised mine 
execution and expanded equipment deployment.
The Power sales volumes were marginally lower on a 
year-on-year basis as a greater proportion of power 
generation was consumed captively to support 
enhanced DRI and Pellet plant operations.
The Company is scaling its renewable energy portfolio 
to 100 MW (120 MW planned) through solar and wind 
power, aimed at reducing its carbon footprint and 
energy costs across operations.
Pellet Manufacturing
FY 2025-26 marked the first full year of commercial 
production from the Company’s 4 MTPA Pellet Plant (Plant – 
1) at Konsari, District Gadchiroli. The Pellet Plant commenced 
commercial production at the end of Q2 FY 2025-26 and 
achieved 100% annualised capacity utilisation within just 4 
months of commissioning – a testament to the Company’s 
swift and efficient project execution.
The Pellet Plant utilise advanced Straight Grate Technology 
and produce high-grade pellets with an iron content 
of ~64.3% Fe, sourced from captive iron ore fines at the 
Surjagarh Iron Ore Mine ("SIOM"). The 85 km slurry pipeline 
(Hedri to Konsari), already operational at 10 MTPA, has been 
instrumental in ensuring consistent, cost-effective, and 
environmentally responsible raw material supply, reducing 
dependence on road logistics and generating freight savings.

Reserves of Iron Ore
The Company’s primary iron ore asset, the SIOM, is located in Maharashtra and spans 348.09 hectares under a 
mining lease valid until 2057. The mine produces high-grade hematite ore with an average iron content of 63% Fe. 
The Company holds a zero-premium payment obligation to the Government of Maharashtra for the entire lease 
period – a significant structural cost advantage relative to the competitors.
Tata Steel Industrial Consulting's Mineral Resource Report estimates a total geological resource of 863 million tonnes 
comprising 157 million tonnes of Direct Shipping Ore ("DSO") and 706 million tonnes of Banded Hematite Quartzite 
("BHQ"). With an expanded EC capacity of 55 MTPA and Lloyds Metals and Energy Limited’s mine lease valid until 
CY2057, the Company is strategically positioned to remain one of India’s leading iron ore miners beyond CY2030. 
This assumes significance as more than 80 MTPA of competing mining capacity across the industry is expected to 
come up for re-auction by CY2030 at comparatively higher auction premiums.

&

FINANCIAL CONTROLS
Management of risk has always been an integral part 
of the Company’s strategy and straddles its planning, 
execution and reporting processes and systems. 
Your Company continues to focus on a system-based 
approach to business risk management.
Our success as an organization depends on our ability to 
identify and leverage the opportunities while managing 
the risks. The Risk Management Committee is constituted 
to frame, implement and monitor the risk management 
plan of the Company. The Risk Management Committee 
of the Company has been entrusted by the Board with the 
responsibility of reviewing the risk management process 
in the Company and ensuring that the risks are brought 
within acceptable limits.
Our approach to risk management is to identify, evaluate 
risks and opportunities. This framework is intended to 
assist in decision making process that will minimise 
potential losses, improve the management in the phase 
of uncertainty and the approach to new opportunities, 
thereby helping the Company to achieve its objectives.
Details of risks & concerns associated with the Company 
has been provided under the Management Discussion 
and Analysis Report.
The Risk Management policy is available on the website 
of the Company at www.lloyds.in/investors/investor-
policies/.
The Company’s internal control systems are tailored to 
the specific nature of its business, as well as the scale 
and intricacy of its operations. These systems undergo 
regular testing by both Statutory and Internal Auditors, 
encompassing all offices, factories, and pivotal business 
domains. The Company has implemented robust 
procedures to ensure the systematic and effective 
management of its operations, encompassing adherence 
to corporate policies, protection of assets, and the 
prevention and detection of fraudulent activities and errors.

DIVIDEND DISTRIBUTION POLICY
This policy applies to the Distribution of Dividend by 
Lloyds Metals and Energy Limited (“the Company”) in 
accordance with the provisions of the Companies Act, 
2013 (“the Act”) and the SEBI (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, (“LODR”) 
as amended.
DEFINITIONS:
The terms referred to in the Policy will have the same 
meaning as defined under the Act, the Rules made there 
under, and the LODR Regulations.
BACKGROUND:
This policy sets out the parameters and circumstances 
that will be taken into account by the Board of Directors 
of the Company in determining the distribution of 
dividend to its Shareholders and/or retaining profits 
earned by the Company.
1. The 
circumstances 
under 
which 
the 
Shareholders 
may 
or 
may 
not 
expect 
Dividend:
	
The Company shall comply with the relevant 
statutory requirements that are applicable to 
the Company in declaring dividend or retained 
earnings. Generally, the Board shall determine the 
dividend for a particular period after taking into 
consideration the financial performance of the 
Company, the advice of Executive Management, 
and other parameters described in this policy.
2. The Financial /Internal parameters that shall 
be considered while declaring Dividend:
	
The Board of Directors of the Company shall 
consider the following financial parameters while 
declaring dividend or recommending dividend to 
the Shareholders:
(a)	 Capital allocation plans including
	
(i)	
Expected cash requirements of the Company 
towards working capital, capital expenditure 
in technology and Infrastructure, general 
corporate purpose etc.;
	
(ii)	 Investments required towards execution of the 
Company’s strategy;
	
(iii)	 Funds required for any acquisitions that the 
Board of Directors may approve; and
	
(iv)	 Any share buy-back plans.
(b)	 Minimum cash required for contingencies or 
unforeseen events;
(c)	 Funds required to service any outstanding loans;
(d)	 Liquidity and return ratios;
(e)	 Any other significant developments that require 
cash investments.
3. External factors that shall be considered for 
declaration of dividend:
	
The Board of Directors of the Company shall 
consider the following external parameters while 
declaring dividend or recommending dividend to 
the Shareholders:
	
(a)	 Any significant changes in macro-economic 
environment affecting India or the geographies 
in which the Company operates, or the 
business of the Company or its clients;
	
(b)	 Any political, tax and regulatory changes in the 
geographies in which the Company operates;
	
(c)	 Any significant change in the business or 
technological environment resulting in the 
Company making significant investments 
to effect the necessary changes to its 
business model;
	
(d)	 Any changes in the competitive environment 
requiring significant investment.
4. Policy as to how the Retained Earnings shall 
be utilized:
	
The consolidated profits earned by the Company 
can either be retained in the business and used for 
various purposes as outlined in clause 2 above or it 
can be distributed to the shareholders.

ANNEXURE - III
ANNUAL REPORT ON CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY ACTIVITIES
[Pursuant to the Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 and Companies  
(Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) Rules, 2014]
1.	 A brief outline of the company’s CSR policy, including overview of projects or programmes 
proposed to be undertaken and a reference to the web-link to the CSR policy and projects 
or programmes:
	
The Company is actively engaged in a wide range of social welfare initiatives aimed at enhancing the quality 
of life for underprivileged communities, particularly in the rural areas surrounding its manufacturing units 
located in the districts of Chandrapur and Gadchiroli, Maharashtra. These initiatives span several critical areas 
of development:
	
(a)	 Promoting Education: The Company promotes education by providing educational support, learning 
resources, scholarships, and other academic assistance to underprivileged students, enabling them to 
pursue educational opportunities that may otherwise be inaccessible. The Company also undertakes 
livelihood enhancement projects aimed at empowering individuals and improving economic self-
sufficiency within local communities.
	
(b)	 Women Empowerment: The Company undertakes initiatives focused on empowering women through 
skill development, awareness programmes, livelihood opportunities, and community participation aimed 
at promoting social and economic inclusion.
	
(c)	 Sports Promotion: To foster physical well-being, discipline, and team spirit among youth, the Company 
organizes local sports tournaments and encourages active participation in sporting activities.
	
(d)	 Clean Water Access and Sanitation: To address the critical need for safe drinking water and improved 
hygiene, the Company is installing water purification systems, developing water facilities in underserved 
villages, and promoting sanitation and cleanliness initiatives for better public health and community well-
being.
	
(e)	 Rural Development Projects: The Company undertakes rural development projects focused on 
infrastructure enhancement, livelihood support, sanitation, accessibility to essential services, and overall 
socio-economic development of rural communities.
	
(f)	
Healthcare: The Company undertakes healthcare initiatives, including preventive healthcare programmes, 
by organising free medical camps to provide basic healthcare services, health awareness, and essential 
medicines to those in need.
	
(g)	 Basic Necessities: Food, clothing, and other essential items are distributed in remote and disadvantaged 
areas to support immediate community needs and improve living conditions.
	
Through these targeted and sustained efforts, the Company remains committed to fostering holistic 
development and enhancing the well-being of the communities it serves. At the heart of the Company’s CSR 
initiatives lies a deep commitment to societal welfare and sustainable development. The Company views its 
contribution not merely as a responsibility, but as a meaningful reflection of its core values, demonstrating its 
dedication to ethical practices, community empowerment, environmental stewardship, and inclusive growth. 
The Company remains steadfast in its mission to create a lasting and positive impact on society.

a)	 Issuance of Securities of the Company through Permissible Modes.
	
The Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held on 25th April, 2025, approved the raising of funds 
through issuance of securities, including equity shares or any other eligible securities, by way of private 
placement, preferential allotment, qualified institutions placement (“QIP”), and/or any other permissible modes 
or combination thereof, in one or more tranches.
	
The aforesaid issuance shall be undertaken in accordance with the applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 
2013, the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, as amended from time to time, 
and other applicable laws, for an aggregate amount not exceeding I 5,000 Crore (Rupees Five Thousand Crore).
b)	 Issuance and allotment of 19,57,458 equity shares of the company on a preferential basis 
for consideration other than cash, towards the acquisition of stake in Thriveni Pellets Private 
Limited by way of a share swap.
	
The Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held on 12th August, 2025, approved the issuance of 
19,57,458 (Nineteen Lakh Fifty-Seven Thousand Four Hundred and Fifty-Eight Only) fully paid-up equity shares 
of face value of I 1 (Rupee One Only) each at an issue price of I 1,460.50 (Rupees One Thousand Four Hundred 
Sixty and Fifty Paise Only) per equity share, including a premium of I 1,459.50 (Rupees One Thousand Four 
Hundred Fifty-Nine and Fifty Paise Only) per share, on a preferential basis to Adler Industrial Services Private 
Limited (“Adler”), a promoter shareholder of Thriveni Pellets Private Limited (“TPPL”).
	
The said issuance was undertaken for an aggregate consideration comprising cash consideration 
of I 200,00,00,000 (Rupees Two Hundred Crores Only) and non-cash consideration of I 2,85,88,67,409 
(Rupees Two Hundred Eighty-Five Crore Eighty-Eight Lakh Sixty-Seven Thousand Four Hundred Nine Only), 
the latter being discharged by way of a share swap in lieu of acquisition of 49% (Forty-Nine percent) of the total 
issued, subscribed and paid-up equity share capital of TPPL from Adler. The aforesaid preferential issue was 
subsequently approved by the shareholders of the Company at the Extraordinary General Meeting held on 11th 
September, 2025. Pursuant to the approval accorded by the shareholders, 19,57,458 equity shares were allotted 
to Adler on 21st October, 2025 vide circular resolution passed by the Board of Directors.
c)	 Issuance of Non-Convertible Debentures
	
The Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held on 12th August, 2025, approved the issuance of Non-
Convertible Debentures (“NCDs”) on a private placement basis for an aggregate amount of up to I 2,000 Crore 
(Rupees Two Thousand Crore), with a greenshoe option of up to I 500 Crore (Rupees Five Hundred Crore).
	
The NCDs may be issued in one or more tranches, depending on market conditions, funding requirements, and 
investor appetite, and shall be governed by the terms of a Debenture Trust Deed.
d)	 Allotment of equity shares pursuant to conversion of convertible warrants
	
The Board of Directors of the Company, at its meetings held on 12th August, 2025, 31st December, 2025, 3rd 
February, 2026 and 13th March, 2026 approved the allotment of 31,00,000, 1,52,68,950, 8,05,500 and 
1,76,20,550 equity shares, respectively, of face value of I 1/- (Rupee One only) each, fully paid-up, out of the 
unissued authorised share capital of the Company.
	
These equity shares were allotted pursuant to the exercise of conversion rights by warrant holders, who 
exercised their option to convert an equivalent number of warrants into equity shares. The Company has 
received the balance exercise price of I 481/- (Rupees Four Hundred and Eighty-One only) per warrant.
	
The aforesaid allotments have been made on a preferential basis to both promoters and non-promoters.

A. CONSERVATION OF ENERGY
(i)	 Steps taken for conservation of energy
	
↘Installation of CO & CO₂ analyser at WHRB Boiler 
1 to 5 outlet has been undertaken for effective 
combustion monitoring and control in kilns 
and boilers. The project enables continuous 
measurement of CO & CO₂ levels at boiler outlet, 
which assists in maintaining proper combustion 
conditions and identifying secondary burning 
at boiler screen tubes. The initiative helps in 
optimizing fuel utilisation by ensuring complete 
combustion, thereby reducing energy losses due 
to unburnt fuel and improving overall thermal 
efficiency of the kiln and boiler operations. The 
project is also expected to ensure smooth boiler 
operation and stable process performance.
The project includes installation of 5 Nos. CO 
analysers along with control systems, power 
and signal cables, GI pipes, pipe fittings, valves, 
MS pipes & flanges, perforated trays and 
commissioning support services.
	
↘The Company has implemented Ripik Raw 
Material Monitoring system for real-time 
monitoring of coal moisture content and size 
distribution to optimise combustion efficiency. 
The system enables operators to instantly 
fine-tune fuel feed rates and kiln combustion 
parameters based on real-time coal quality data.
The initiative facilitates identification of wet 
or oversized coal at an early stage, enabling 
immediate corrective action and ensuring stable 
and efficient combustion. Real-time sizing 
data ensures feeding of the correct coal size 
fraction into the kiln at the required rate, thereby 
improving combustion efficiency, reducing 
excess fuel consumption, minimising heat losses 
and eliminating dependency on delayed manual 
sampling reports.

evolving to meet the demands of a dynamic business

practices against global standards, strengthen Board

ensure resilience and long-term sustainability. Governance

institutional credibility, and position the Company to lead 
with discipline, foresight, and integrity in an increasingly 
complex and competitive landscape.

of integrity, accountability, and

Board Composition
The Company is in compliance with the provisions of 
Section 149 of the Companies Act, 2013 (“the Act”) and 
Regulation 17 of the Listing Regulations with regard to the 
composition of the Board.
The Board comprises an optimal mix of Executive and 
Non-executive Directors, bringing together diverse 
expertise, experience, and independent judgment. As on 
date, the Board consists of 15 (Fifteen) Directors, including 
Executive and Non-executive members, with adequate 
representation of Independent Directors, including 2 (Two) 
Women Independent Directors. Of the total strength 
4 (Four) Directors are Executive Directors and 11 (Eleven) 
Directors are Non-executive, out of which 8 (Eight) are 
Independent Directors, thereby ensuring a strong element 
of independence in Board deliberations.
The Chairperson of the Company is a Promoter and Non-
executive Director. Accordingly, in line with regulatory 
requirements, at least half of the Board comprises of 
Independent Directors, ensuring balanced governance 
and objective oversight.
All Independent Directors have confirmed that they meet 
the criteria of independence as prescribed under Section 
149 of the Act and Regulation 16(1)(b) of the Listing 
Regulations. They have further affirmed compliance with 
Regulation 25(8) of the Listing Regulations, confirming that 
no circumstances exist which may impair, or potentially 
impair, their ability to discharge duties with independence 
and objectivity.
In the Board’s opinion, the Independent Directors 
meet the conditions of independence set out in the Act 
and the Listing Regulations and are independent of 
the Management.
In accordance with Section 150 of the Act read with Rule 
6 of the Companies (Appointment and Qualification 
of Directors) Rules, 2014, the Independent Directors 
have confirmed their registration with the Independent 
Directors’ databank maintained by the Indian Institute of 
Corporate Affairs. The Board has taken these declarations 
on record.
None of the Independent Directors holds office as an 
Independent Director in more than 7 (Seven) listed 
companies or 3 (Three) listed companies if serving as a 
Whole-time Director or Managing Director in any other 
listed company, as required under Regulation 17A of the 
Listing Regulations. Additionally, the Executive Director(s) 
of the Company are not serving as Independent Directors 
in any listed company. Furthermore, none of the Directors 
holds directorship in more than 20 (Twenty) Indian 
companies, with no more than 10 (Ten) being public 
limited companies.
In the opinion of the Board, the Independent Directors fulfil 
the conditions specified in the Listing Regulations and are 
independent from the management.
All Directors have made the necessary disclosures regarding 
their directorships in other companies, as required under 
Section 184 of the Act, and the positions held in committees 
across other companies, as stipulated under Regulation 
26 of the Listing Regulations. None of the Directors is a 
member of more than 10 (Ten) committees or acts as the 
chairperson of more than 5 (Five) committees (including 
the Audit Committee and the Stakeholders' Relationship 
Committee), as specified under Regulation 26(1) of the 
Listing Regulations, across all public limited companies in 
which they serve as Directors.
Overall, the Board composition reflects a balanced structure 
with an appropriate mix of skills, experience, independence, 
and diversity, enabling effective oversight, informed 
decision-making, and strong governance practices.

4. Board Procedures & Flow of Information
	
The Board is committed to ensuring that its members 
have timely access to complete, accurate, and 
relevant information to enable informed and effective 
decision-making. A structured and robust framework 
governs the flow of information to the Board and its 
Committees, ensuring transparency, consistency, and 
quality in all deliberations.
	
The Company Secretary plays a central role in 
facilitating the Board’s functioning and is responsible 
for the collation, review, and dissemination of all 
agenda papers and supporting documents. In 
consultation with the Managing Director and Chief 
Financial Officer, the Company Secretary finalises the 
agenda for each meeting, ensuring that all critical 
business matters are appropriately placed before 
the Board, supported by comprehensive explanatory 
notes. Inputs and suggestions from Directors and 
Committee Members are actively sought and 
incorporated, fostering an inclusive and participative 
decision-making process.
	
Board and Committee meetings are scheduled well 
in advance, enabling Directors to effectively plan their 
participation. Detailed agenda papers are circulated 
within a reasonable timeframe prior to the meetings, 
allowing adequate time for review and preparation. 
This structured approach ensures that discussions are 
meaningful, focused, and outcome-oriented.
	
The Board is regularly apprised of key developments 
across all aspects of the Company’s operations, 
including strategic initiatives, financial performance, 
risk management, compliance status, and 
sustainability matters. In accordance with Regulation 
17(7) read with Schedule II of the Listing Regulations, 
the Company continually endeavours to enhance the 
quality, depth, and timeliness of information shared 
with the Board.
	
In situations requiring urgent consideration, decisions 
are taken through resolutions passed by circulation, in 
compliance with applicable provisions of the Act. Such 
resolutions are subsequently noted and recorded at 
the ensuing Board meeting, ensuring transparency 
and continuity in governance.
	
The Company Secretary attends all Board and 
Committee meetings and ensures the accurate 
recording of proceedings. Draft minutes are circulated 
to all members for their review and comments 
in compliance with the Secretarial Standards on 
Meetings of the Board of Directors (“SS-1”) issued 
by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India 
(“ICSI”). Upon incorporation of suggestions, the final 
minutes are entered in the minute’s books within the 
prescribed timelines, ensuring proper documentation 
and institutional memory.
	
The Company strictly adheres to the provisions of the 
Act, the Rules made thereunder, applicable Secretarial 
Standards, and the Listing Regulations with respect 
to convening and conducting Board, Committee, 
and General Meetings. The required quorum was 
present at all meetings, and the gap between two 
consecutive meetings did not exceed the statutory 
limit of 120 days.
	
An effective post-meeting follow-up mechanism is in 
place to track the implementation of decisions taken 
by the Board and its Committees. Action points arising 
from meetings are systematically monitored, and 
status updates are presented in subsequent meetings, 
ensuring accountability and timely execution.
	
Further, Directors have unrestricted access to senior 
management and are provided with the opportunity 
to seek external professional advice, where necessary, 
at the Company’s expense. This strengthens 
independent judgment and enhances the overall 
quality of Board deliberations.

7. Familiarization Program: From 
Awareness to Insight
	
In accordance with the provisions of Section 149 read 
with Schedule IV (Part III) of the Act and Regulation 
25 of the Listing Regulation, the Company has 
established a structured Familiarization Programme 
for Independent Directors.
	
The programme is designed to provide both initial 
induction and continuous updates, enabling 
Independent Directors to gain a comprehensive 
understanding of the Company’s business, operations, 
industry dynamics, and governance framework. 
It equips them with the necessary knowledge to 
effectively discharge their roles and responsibilities.
	
Upon appointment, Independent Directors are 
provided with a detailed induction programme that 
familiarises them with the Company’s history, vision 
and values, organisational structure, business model, 
and financial performance. The programme also 
covers key areas such as:
	
(i)	
Corporate Governance – Roles, responsibilities, 
and functioning of the Board and its Committees.
	
(ii)	
Risk Management – Overview of key business 
risks and the framework for identification, 
monitoring, and mitigation.
	
(iii)	 Regulatory Compliance – Applicable 
legal and regulatory requirements and 
governance standards.
	
(iv)	 Business Operations & Strategy – Insights into 
operational processes, strategic priorities, and 
growth plans.
	
(v)	 Organisational Culture – Values, leadership 
philosophy, and employee engagement practices.
	
During the year, the Company conducted a 
Corporate Training Programme for Directors on 
the topic “Corporate Governance and the Role of 
Independent Directors.” The session was led by a 
renowned professional with over four decades of 
experience, providing valuable insights into evolving 
governance practices, regulatory expectations, 
and the critical role of Independent Directors in 
strengthening Board effectiveness.
	
The programme facilitated meaningful discussions 
and enhanced the Directors’ understanding 
of governance frameworks, enabling them to 
contribute more effectively to Board deliberations and 
oversight functions.
	
In addition to the formal induction, the Company 
conducts ongoing familiarization through presentations 
and interactions during Board and Committee 
meetings. These sessions cover business performance, 
strategic initiatives, operational developments, market 
dynamics, financial results, and emerging risks. This 
continuous engagement ensures that Independent 
Directors remain updated and are able to contribute 
meaningfully to deliberations and decision-making.
	
Independent Directors are also encouraged to engage 
with senior management and, where appropriate, 
undertake site visits and operational reviews to 
gain deeper insights into the Company’s business 
and functioning.
	
These initiatives collectively ensure that Independent 
Directors are well-informed, enabling them to provide 
independent judgment, constructive challenge, and 
strategic guidance to the management.
	
The suggestions of the discussion where collated by 
the Chairperson of Independent Director Meeting 
and were shared with the Company Secretary and the 
same were discussed with.
	
The evaluation outcomes were discussed by the 
Nomination and Remuneration Committee and the 
Board, and appropriate actions, where considered 
necessary, are being implemented to further enhance 
Board effectiveness and governance standards.
	
The policy on performance evaluation of the Board, 
its Committees, and Directors is available on the 
Company’s website at www.lloyds.in/investors/
investor-policies/. 
A robust evaluation framework 
drives continuous improvement 
and strengthens the 
effectiveness of the Board and 
its governance practices
9. Leadership Continuity & Succession 
Framework
	
Succession planning is a key pillar of the Company’s 
long-term strategy, focused on ensuring leadership 
continuity, organisational resilience, and sustained 
business performance. The Company has established 
a structured and forward-looking succession planning 
framework to identify, develop, and retain talent for 
critical leadership roles, thereby mitigating risks 
associated with leadership transitions.
	
The framework encompasses the systematic 
identification of key positions across the organisation, 
assessment of internal talent, and creation of a robust 
leadership pipeline. High-potential employees are 
identified through performance evaluations and 
leadership assessments and are supported through 
targeted development initiatives, cross-functional 
exposure, mentoring, and leadership development 
programmes to prepare them for future roles.
	
The Nomination and Remuneration Committee, along 
with the Board, oversees the succession planning 
process, ensuring that it remains aligned with the 
Company’s strategic priorities and evolving business 
environment. The framework is reviewed periodically 
to assess its effectiveness, identify potential gaps, 
and incorporate improvements based on changing 
organisational needs and external developments.
	
The details of the Familiarization Programme 
imparted to Independent Directors are available on 
the Company’s website and can be accessed at: www.
lloyds.in/investors/investor-policies/
Such initiatives reflect the 
Company’s commitment 
to continuous learning and 
strengthening governance 
capabilities at the Board level.
8. Board Effectiveness & Evaluation 
Framework
	
The Nomination and Remuneration Committee, 
in consultation with the Board, has laid down a 
comprehensive framework and criteria for the 
evaluation of the performance of the Board, its 
Committees, and individual Directors, including 
Independent Directors, in accordance with the 
provisions of the Act and the Listing Regulations.
	
Pursuant to these requirements, the Board undertook 
an annual evaluation of its own performance, the 
functioning of its Committees, and the performance 
of individual Directors. The evaluation process 
was carried out through a structured mechanism, 
designed to assess various aspects of Board 
effectiveness, including composition, diversity, quality 
of deliberations, strategic oversight, governance 
practices, and the effectiveness of decision-making.
	
The evaluation was conducted through detailed 
questionnaires, in line with the Guidance Note on 
Board Evaluation issued by SEBI (dated January 5, 
2017). Directors provided their feedback on multiple 
parameters such as Board dynamics, participation 
levels, quality and timeliness of information, Committee 
effectiveness, and overall governance framework.
	
The feedback received was collated and analysed, 
and the outcome of the evaluation indicated a high 
level of effectiveness in the functioning of the Board 
and its Committees. The process also facilitated 
constructive insights and suggestions for further 
strengthening governance practices and enhancing 
Board performance.
	
The Independent Directors, in a separate meeting, 
also reviewed the performance of the Chairperson, 
the Non-Independent Directors, and the Board as a 
whole, in accordance with the applicable provisions 
of the Act.

11. Code of Conduct & Ethical Standards
	
Pursuant to Regulation 17(5)(a) of the Listing 
Regulations, the Company has adopted a 
comprehensive Code of Conduct applicable to its 
Directors, Key Managerial Personnel (“KMP”) and 
Senior Management Personnel (“SMP”). The Code 
sets out the principles of integrity, ethical behaviour, 
transparency, and accountability that govern the 
conduct of business and decision-making across 
the organisation.
	
The Code is designed to ensure that members of the 
Board and Senior Management uphold the highest 
standards of professional and ethical conduct 
while discharging their duties. It also reinforces the 
Company’s commitment to fair practices, regulatory 
compliance, and responsible corporate citizenship.
	
All Directors, KMP and SMP have affirmed their

review. In addition, pursuant to Regulation 26(5) of the 
Listing Regulations. All Directors, KMP and SMP have

objectivity and impartiality in decision-making.

Annexure I.
	
The Code of Conduct is available on the Company’s 
website at www.lloyds.in/investors/investor-policies/.
12. Insider Trading – Code of Conduct
	
In accordance with the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider 
Trading) Regulations, 2015, as amended from time to 
time, the Company has (“PIT Regulations”) adopted a 
comprehensive Code of Conduct to regulate, monitor, 
and report trading by Designated Persons and their 
immediate relatives.
	
The Code is aimed at preserving the integrity of 
the securities market by preventing the misuse of 
Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (“UPSI”). It 
ensures that persons in possession of UPSI do not 
trade in the Company’s securities or communicate 
such information, directly or indirectly, for personal 
gain or to the detriment of shareholders.
	
The Company has established a well-defined 
framework for the identification, handling, and control 
of UPSI, including maintaining a structured digital 
database of persons with whom such information 
is shared. Adequate internal controls, confidentiality 
protocols, and access restrictions are in place to ensure 
that UPSI is handled strictly on a need-to-know basis.
	
As part of its governance practices, the Company has 
implemented a robust trading window mechanism, 
which remains closed during specified periods, 
including around the declaration of financial results 
and the occurrence of material events. During such 
periods, Designated Persons and their immediate 
relatives are prohibited from trading in the Company’s 
securities. Further, pre-clearance of trades is mandated 
for transactions beyond prescribed thresholds.
	
Pursuant to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/ISD/ISD-PoD-
2/P/CIR/2025/55, read with the Master Circular on 
Surveillance of Securities Market, the Company has 
also implemented the system-enabled mechanism 
for restricting trading by Designated Persons and 
Immediate Relatives during the trading window 
closure period. In line with the prescribed framework, 
the Company provides necessary details of Designated 
Persons and Immediate Relatives to the Depositories, 
enabling the freezing of their PAN at the security level 
during such closure periods. This automated control 
mechanism further strengthens compliance with 
Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of the 
PIT Regulations and mitigates the risk of inadvertent 
non-compliance.
	
The Company Secretary acts as the Compliance 
Officer under the Regulations and is responsible for 
administering the Code, monitoring adherence, and 
ensuring compliance with applicable provisions. The 
Compliance Officer also oversees pre-clearance of 
trades, maintenance of records, and timely disclosures 
to the stock exchanges as may be applicable.
	
The Company undertakes periodic awareness and 
sensitization programmes to ensure that Designated 
Persons are fully aware of their obligations under the 
Code and applicable regulatory requirements.
	
Any violations of the Code are dealt with strictly in 
accordance with applicable regulatory provisions and 
the Company’s internal policies, reinforcing a zero-
tolerance approach towards insider trading.
	
The Insider Trading – Code of Conduct is available on 
the Company’s website at www.lloyds.in/investors/
investor-policies/.
The Company remains steadfast 
in its commitment to preventing 
misuse of unpublished price 
sensitive information and 
upholding the highest standards 
of integrity, fairness, and 
transparency in securities trading

The Audit Committee plays a pivotal role in strengthening 
the Company’s financial governance framework by 
ensuring transparency, integrity, and accountability in 
financial reporting and internal control processes. The 
Committee provides focused oversight on financial 
disclosures, statutory and internal audit functions, risk 
management practices, internal financial controls, 
related party transactions, and compliance with legal and 
regulatory requirements.
The composition of the Audit Committee is in conformity 
with the requirements of Section 177 of the Act and 
Regulation 18 of the Listing Regulation, as on 31st March, 
2026. The Committee comprises Directors possessing 
strong financial, accounting, and governance expertise, 
enabling effective and informed oversight.
The Chairperson of the Audit Committee is an Independent 
Director, and the majority of the Members are Independent 
Directors, ensuring objectivity and independence in the 
functioning of the Committee. The Company Secretary 
acts as the Secretary to the Committee.
The Committee functions within a clearly defined Terms 
of Reference approved by the Board, which is aligned with 
statutory and regulatory requirements and is periodically 
reviewed to reflect evolving governance expectations and 
best practices.
The Audit Committee serves as an important link between 
the Board, the Statutory Auditors, Internal Auditors, and 
the Management, facilitating open discussions and 
constructive engagement on matters relating to financial 
reporting, audit observations, compliance, and internal 
controls. Representatives of the Statutory Auditors, Internal 
Auditors, and Senior Management are invited to attend the 
meetings, as required, to provide clarifications and insights 
on matters placed before the Committee.
The Committee also reviews the adequacy and 
effectiveness of the internal control environment and 
monitors the implementation of audit recommendations 
to strengthen governance processes and operational 
discipline across the organisation.
The maximum gap between any two meetings of the Audit 
Committee during the Financial Year under review did not 
exceed 120 days, in compliance with Regulation 18 of the 
Listing Regulations.
The Chairman, Managing Director, and Chief Financial 
Officer are permanent invitees to the meetings of the Audit 
Committee. In addition, representatives of the Statutory 
Auditors, Internal Auditors, and senior executives, as 
considered necessary, are invited to attend the meetings 
to provide clarifications, insights, and professional inputs 
on matters placed before the Committee.
The presence of KMP and auditors facilitates transparent 
discussions, comprehensive financial review, and effective 
oversight of the Company’s financial reporting, internal 
control systems, risk management framework, and 
compliance processes.
The Chairperson of the Audit Committee attended the 48th 
Annual General Meeting (“AGM” ) of the Company held on 
2nd June, 2025, and was available to address queries and 
provide clarifications to the Members relating to matters 
within the scope of the Committee’s responsibilities.

enough to cover the role specified for Audit Committee 
under Section 177 of the Act and Regulation 18 of the 
Listing Regulations. The same are constantly reviewed 
and appropriate changes are made from time to time 
for greater effectiveness of the Committee. The terms of 
reference of the Committee are as follows:

Composition of the Stakeholders’ Relationship Committee
The Stakeholders’ Relationship Committee (“SRC”) plays 
a significant role in strengthening investor confidence 
and fostering transparent and responsive stakeholder 
engagement. The Committee oversees and monitors 
the timely and effective resolution of grievances of 
shareholders, debenture holders, and other security 
holders, thereby reinforcing accountability, fairness, and 
stakeholder trust.
The Committee specifically reviews matters relating to 
transfer and transmission of securities, non-receipt of 
annual reports, dividends and interest, issue of duplicate 
certificates, dematerialisation and rematerialisation 
requests, investor correspondence, and other stakeholder-
related concerns that may arise from time to time.
In addition to grievance redressal, the SRC actively reviews 
adherence to the service standards adopted by the 
Registrar and Share Transfer Agent (“RTA”) and monitors 
the effectiveness of investor servicing mechanisms. The 
Committee also reviews measures undertaken by the 
Company to facilitate the effective exercise of voting rights 
by shareholders and initiatives aimed at reducing the 
quantum of unclaimed dividends. Further, the Committee 
oversees processes to ensure timely receipt of dividend 
warrants, Annual Reports, statutory notices, and other 
communications by shareholders.
The Committee periodically reviews the status of investor 
grievances, pending requests, and compliance with 
applicable regulatory requirements relating to investor 
services and stakeholder communication. It works closely 
with the RTA and the Management to ensure seamless 
investor interface and efficient stakeholder servicing.
The composition of the SRC is in conformity with the 
requirements of Section 178 of the Act and Regulation 
20 of the Listing Regulations, as on 31st March, 2026. The 
majority of the Members of the Committee are Independent 
Directors, ensuring objective and independent oversight.
The Chairperson of the SRC attended the 48th AGM 
of the Company held on 2nd June, 2025, and and was 
available to address queries and provide clarifications to 
the Members relating to matters within the scope of the 
Committee’s responsibilities.

Section 178 of the Act and Regulation 20 of the Listing 
Regulations. The Committee, inter alia, is primarily 
responsible for considering and resolving grievances of

reference of the Committee are as follows:

listed entity including complaints related to transfer/

INVESTOR SUPPORT & GRIEVANCE 
MANAGEMENT
The Company places significant emphasis on 
maintaining transparent, responsive, and investor-
centric communication with its shareholders and other 
stakeholders. An effective grievance redressal framework 
has been established to ensure that investor concerns are 
addressed promptly, efficiently, and in a fair manner.
The SRC of the Board has been entrusted with the 
responsibility of reviewing, monitoring, and resolving 
complaints and queries received from Members, debenture 
holders, and other security holders. The Committee 
periodically reviews the status of investor grievances, 
requests, and compliance-related matters and reports the 
same to the Board on a quarterly basis, thereby ensuring 
continuous oversight, accountability, and improvement in 
investor servicing standards.
The Company, in coordination with its RTA, Bigshare 
Services Private Limited, actively monitors complaints and 
investor requests through the SEBI Complaints Redressal 
System (“SCORES”) to facilitate timely and effective 
resolution of grievances. The Company has implemented 
processes and controls to ensure that investor complaints 
are resolved within the timelines prescribed by SEBI and 
other applicable regulatory authorities.
In addition to grievance redressal, the Company 
continuously endeavours to enhance investor experience 
through proactive communication, simplified processes, 
timely dissemination of information, and seamless 
shareholder servicing. The Company remains committed 
to protecting investor interests and strengthening 
stakeholder confidence through transparent and 
responsive engagement practices.
Mr. Akshay Vora, Company Secretary, acts as the 
Compliance Officer of the Company. For the convenience 
of shareholders, debenture holders and investors, the 
Company has established a dedicated investor grievance 
e-mail mechanism at investor@lloyds.in to facilitate prompt 
electronic communication and resolution of concerns.
In compliance with SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/OIAE/OIAE_
IAD-1/P/CIR/2023/131 dated 31st July, 2023, the Company 
has also registered itself on the Smart Online Dispute 
Resolution System (“ODR Portal”), a technology-enabled 
platform introduced by SEBI for online conciliation and 
arbitration of investor disputes. This mechanism further 
strengthens the Company’s investor grievance redressal 
framework by providing shareholders with an additional 
transparent and efficient dispute resolution avenue.
Relevant investor contact details, shareholder service 
information, and access links relating to grievance redressal 
mechanisms, including the ODR Portal, are available on the 
Company’s website under the Investor Relations section.
During the Financial Year under review, the Company and 
its RTA received complaints and investor queries from 
SEBI, Stock Exchanges, and Members. Majority of the 
complaints received during the year were resolved within 
the timelines prescribed under the applicable regulations. 
The complaints remaining unresolved as on 31st March, 
2026 primarily pertained to matters received towards the 
close of the financial year and were under active resolution 
process as detailed below:

SPECIAL INVESTOR OUTREACH & 
SHAREHOLDER SERVICE INITIATIVES
During the Financial Year 2025-26, the Company undertook 
several investor-focused initiatives in line with regulatory 
developments and shareholder facilitation measures 
introduced by the Securities and Exchange Board of India 
(“SEBI”), the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (“MCA”), and the 
Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority (“IEPF 
Authority”). These initiatives were reviewed by the SRC 
as part of its oversight on investor servicing, shareholder 
engagement, and regulatory compliance mechanisms.
Special Window for Re-lodgement of Transfer 
Requests of Physical Shares
Pursuant to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-
PoD/P/CIR/2025/97 dated 2nd July, 2025, SEBI introduced 
a special window for re-lodgement of transfer requests 
pertaining to physical shares. The special window remained 
open for a period of 6 (Six) months from 7th July, 2025 to 
January 6, 2026.
In compliance with the aforesaid circular, the Company, in 
coordination with its RTA, facilitated the processing of all 
eligible re-lodged transfer requests through the prescribed 
transfer-cum-dematerialisation process. The Company 
also ensured timely submission of monthly reports in the 
format prescribed by SEBI to the regulatory authorities and 
stock exchanges within the stipulated timelines.
Further, in continuation of the aforesaid investor 
facilitation measures, SEBI introduced another special 
window for transfer and dematerialisation of physical 
securities which were sold or purchased prior to 1st April, 
2019. Accordingly, a fresh special window was opened 
for a period of 1 (One) year from 5th February, 2026 to 
4th February, 2027 to enable investors to re-lodge transfer 
requests pertaining to physical securities.
The said special window is also applicable to transfer 
requests that were earlier rejected, returned, or kept 
pending due to deficiencies in documentation, procedural 
requirements, or related matters. In accordance with the 
prescribed regulatory framework, securities transferred 
pursuant to the said mechanism are mandatorily credited 
only in dematerialised form to the transferee’s demat 
account and remain subject to a lock-in period of 1 (One) 
year from the date of transfer.
The Company, in coordination with its RTA, undertook 
necessary investor awareness and facilitation measures 
to ensure smooth processing of eligible transfer-cum-
dematerialisation requests under the aforesaid special 
window mechanisms.
The SRC periodically reviewed the implementation status 
of the special window mechanisms, including investor 
requests processed, operational preparedness, investor 
facilitation measures undertaken, and compliance 
with the reporting requirements prescribed under the 
SEBI circulars.
Participation in the “Saksham Niveshak” 
Campaign
The Company actively participated in the “Saksham 
Niveshak” investor awareness initiative launched by the 
Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority (“IEPF 
Authority”) pursuant to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs 
(“MCA”) Notification (E-File No. 30/06/2025-IEPFA) dated 
16th July, 2025.
In line with the said initiative, the Company launched a 
dedicated shareholder awareness campaign titled “Don’t 
Delay, Claim Today” from 28th July, 2025 to 6th November, 
2025, aimed at facilitating shareholder awareness, KYC 
updation, claim assistance, and completion of pending 
investor-related compliances.
Through the “Don’t Delay, Claim Today” initiative, the 
Company actively encouraged shareholders to safeguard 
and claim their rightful investments, dividends, and related 
benefits by completing pending KYC formalities, updating 
nomination details, and resolving unclaimed investor-
related matters in a timely manner. The campaign was 
designed to create greater investor awareness regarding 
the importance of maintaining updated records and 
taking proactive steps to prevent transfer of unpaid or 
unclaimed dividends and shares to the Investor Education 
and Protection Fund (“IEPF”).
As part of this initiative, the Company urged Members to 
regularly review their investment records, update PAN, bank 
account, nomination, and contact details, and promptly 
initiate claims relating to unpaid dividends or shares, 
wherever applicable. Through focused communication 
and investor outreach efforts, the Company sought to 
ensure that Members are able to exercise and protect their 
rights seamlessly and without procedural difficulties.
As part of the campaign, the Company undertook various 
outreach and communication initiatives, including:
Hosting detailed investor guidance and 
campaign-related disclosures on the 
Company’s website;
Publication of newspaper advertisements 
for wider shareholder outreach; and
Dissemination of awareness 
communication through digital and 
professional networking platforms;
Sending email communications to 
shareholders whose email addresses were 
registered with the Company.

Lloyds Infinite Foundation
The Lloyds Infinite Foundation (“LIF/Foundation”), a 
wholly owned subsidiary of the Company incorporated 
under Section 8 of the Act serves as the cornerstone of 
the Company’s CSR framework. Established with a vision 
to drive inclusive and sustainable development, the 
Foundation acts as a dedicated platform for implementing 
impactful social initiatives aimed at improving the quality 
of life across underserved and tribal regions, particularly 
in Maharashtra.
Guided by the philosophy of creating long-term social 
value, LIF focuses on initiatives that promote education, 
healthcare, livelihood generation, skill development, 
women empowerment, rural infrastructure, environmental 
sustainability, sports development, and community well-
being. The Foundation’s approach is centred on creating 
sustainable ecosystems that empower communities to 
become self-reliant and economically resilient.
In the field of education, LIF has undertaken transformative 
initiatives aimed at improving access to quality learning 
opportunities in remote and underserved regions. The 
Foundation has established and supported educational 
institutions including CBSE-affiliated schools in 
Chandrapur and Gadchiroli districts, providing students 
with modern educational infrastructure, holistic 
development opportunities, and a strong academic 
foundation. LIF has also supported initiatives focused on 
technical education, vocational learning, and industry-
oriented skill enhancement programmes to improve 
employability and future readiness among youth.
In healthcare, the Foundation has established healthcare 
facilities in Gadchiroli district to improve access to quality 
medical services in tribal and rural areas. Through hospitals, 
healthcare camps, blood donation drives, nutrition and 
wellness initiatives, and preventive healthcare programmes, 
LIF continues to strengthen healthcare accessibility and 
community well-being in regions where quality healthcare 
infrastructure remains limited. The Foundation has also 
undertaken specialised healthcare initiatives, including 
vaccination drives and support towards advanced medical 
infrastructure development.
Further strengthening its focus on livelihood generation 
and economic empowerment, LIF has established 
livelihood and skill development initiatives aimed at 
empowering local communities, particularly tribal 
youth and women. The garment manufacturing unit 
established at Hedri Village, Gadchiroli, has generated 
employment opportunities for local communities and 
contributed towards stimulating economic activity across 
nearby villages. The Foundation also collaborates with 
institutions and organisations to undertake vocational 
training and skill development programmes in areas 
such as welding, electrical work, and industrial trades, 
thereby enhancing employability and creating sustainable 
livelihood opportunities.
LIF also actively promotes women empowerment, youth 
engagement, and sports development through various 
initiatives designed to foster confidence, leadership, 
and social inclusion. The Foundation has supported 
sports academies, athletic development programmes, 
educational camps, environmental awareness campaigns, 
and community development activities that contribute 
towards holistic social progress.
The Foundation places significant emphasis on human 
capital development through skill enhancement, capacity 
building, and community empowerment initiatives. 
Its programmes are designed to build self-confidence, 
improve communication and interpersonal skills, foster 
financial independence, and encourage self-reliance 
among beneficiaries. Through structured training, 
awareness programmes, stipends, and livelihood support 
initiatives, LIF seeks to create meaningful and lasting social 
impact that extends beyond immediate assistance.
The Foundation also encourages community participation 
and collaborative engagement to ensure that its initiatives 
remain inclusive, need-based, and sustainable. Its 
programmes are designed not only to address present-
day challenges but also to create long-term developmental 
outcomes that contribute meaningfully to societal progress 
and regional transformation.
The impactful work undertaken by the Foundation 
has received recognition at various forums. During the 
year, LIF was honoured with the ICC Social Impact 
Award 2026 in the Rural Development category for its 
contribution towards community development and rural 
transformation initiatives in Gadchiroli district.
Through the efforts of LIF, the Company continues to 
reaffirm its belief that sustainable corporate growth must 
go hand in hand with social progress and community 
development. The Foundation stands as a reflection of 
the Company’s enduring commitment to creating positive, 
measurable, and lasting impact across the communities 
it serves.
Through Lloyds Infinite Foundation, 
the Company continues to 
create meaningful social impact 
by empowering communities, 
transforming lives, and building a 
more inclusive and sustainable future.

e.	 Disclosure of commodity price risks, 
foreign exchange risk and hedging 
activities
	
The Company is exposed to commodity price risk 
arising from fluctuations in the prices of key raw 
materials integral to its manufacturing operations. 
These price movements are influenced by global 
supply-demand dynamics, geopolitical developments, 
macroeconomic conditions, and currency volatility 
factors that are largely beyond the Company’s direct 
control. The Company proactively mitigates this risk 
through strategic procurement planning, maintaining 
optimal inventory levels, and where feasible, entering 
into fixed-price or long-term supply arrangements 
with key vendors. The Company does not currently 
engage in exchange-traded commodity derivative 
contracts for hedging purposes.
	
In the ordinary course of business, the Company is 
exposed to foreign exchange risk primarily on two 
counts i.e. import of key raw materials, the prices of 
which are denominated in foreign currency, and 
export of finished products, the proceeds of which are 
receivable in foreign currency. Adverse movements 
in exchange rates between the transaction date 
and settlement date can impact the Company's 
financial performance. To manage these exposures 
prudently, the Company employs a structured 
approach comprising natural hedging, by offsetting 
foreign currency receivables against payables to the 
extent possible, and selectively entering into forward 
foreign exchange contracts for residual exposures 
over and above the natural hedge position. Majority 
hedging activities are undertaken solely for the 
purpose of risk mitigation and not for speculation, in 
accordance with the Company's Board-approved risk 
management framework.
	
The details of foreign currency exposures as at the year-
end, including currency-wise hedged and unhedged 
positions and the fair value of outstanding derivative 
instruments, are disclosed in the Notes to the Financial 
Statements forming part of this Annual Report.

k.	 Commitment to Diversity, Equality, and 
Prevention of Sexual Harassment
	
The Company firmly believes that a diverse, inclusive, 
and respectful workplace is not merely a compliance 
requirement but a cornerstone of sustainable 
organisational growth. The Company is committed to 
fostering a work environment that upholds the values 
of diversity, equality, mutual respect, and dignity for 
every individual irrespective of gender, religion, caste, 
nationality, age, or any other characteristic. Equal 
opportunity is provided to all employees across all 
levels of the organisation, and discrimination of any 
form is strictly prohibited.
	
Prevention of Sexual Harassment
	
In accordance with the provisions of the Sexual 
Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, 
Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (“POSH Act”) 
and the Rules framed thereunder, the Company 
has adopted a comprehensive Policy on Prevention, 
Prohibition and Redressal of Sexual Harassment 
(“POSH Policy”). The Policy is applicable to all women 
employees, including permanent, contractual, 
temporary employees, trainees, interns, and any 
woman associated with the Company in any capacity, 
across all work locations and working environments, 
including remote, virtual, and off-site workplaces.
	
In line with its commitment to providing a safe, 
secure, and respectful workplace, the Company 
has constituted an Internal Complaints Committee 
(“ICC”) in compliance with the provisions of the 
POSH Act. The ICC comprises members possessing 
the requisite experience, sensitivity, and expertise 
to address matters relating to workplace sexual 
harassment, and includes an independent external 
member as mandated under the POSH Act to ensure 
objectivity, neutrality, and fairness in the complaint 
resolution process.
	
The ICC is empowered to receive, inquire into, and 
redress complaints of sexual harassment in a prompt, 
confidential, impartial, and time-bound manner, 
while ensuring adherence to the principles of natural 
justice. The Company follows a zero-tolerance 
approach towards any form of sexual harassment 
and is committed to ensuring that every complaint 
is handled with utmost seriousness, sensitivity, 
and confidentiality.
	
The Company has also established an anonymous whistle blower mechanism through which any woman facing or 
witnessing a POSH-related incident may report concerns through multiple channels, including telephone, email, 
letter, or web-based reporting mechanisms. Such complaints are immediately escalated to the external ICC member 
and, wherever required, investigated in coordination with the internal ICC members to ensure an independent, fair, 
and unbiased inquiry process.
	
Further, compliance with the POSH Policy and adherence to respectful workplace behaviour are reinforced through 
the Company’s Code of Conduct, which expressly emphasises zero tolerance towards any form of sexual harassment 
or misconduct.
	
To strengthen awareness and promote a culture of dignity and mutual respect at the workplace, the Company 
periodically conducts employee awareness programmes, sensitisation workshops, and training sessions for 
employees and ICC members. These initiatives are aimed at educating employees about their rights and 
responsibilities under the POSH Act, the Company’s grievance redressal mechanism, and the importance of 
maintaining an inclusive and respectful work environment.
	
During the Financial Year 2025-26, 1 (One) program was conducted for internal ICC Members and 1 (One) program 
for the employees.

Means of Communication
	
The Company believes that timely, transparent, 
and consistent communication is fundamental to 
maintaining strong relationships with shareholders, 
investors, analysts, regulatory authorities, and other 
stakeholders. Guided by the principles of transparency, 
accountability, and fair disclosure, the Company 
ensures that all material information and corporate 
developments are disseminated promptly and 
accurately in compliance with the Listing Regulations 
and other applicable regulatory requirements.
	
The Company has established a robust communication 
framework to facilitate effective dissemination of 
information through multiple channels, thereby 
ensuring equal, timely, and widespread access to 
corporate information for all stakeholders.
	
The key communication channels adopted by the 
Company include:
	
(i)	
Uploading disclosures and filings on the online 
portals of the Stock Exchanges;
	
(ii)	
Publication of financial results and statutory 
disclosures in newspapers;
	
(iii)	 Issuance of press releases, investor presentations, 
and corporate announcements;
	
(iv)	 Dissemination of information through the 
Company’s official website;
	
(v)	
Conducting investor and analyst interactions and 
conference calls; and
	
(vi)	 Dedicated investor communication and 
grievance redressal mechanisms.
	
This multi-channel approach ensures that stakeholders 
have access to accurate and up-to-date information at 
all times.
	
(i)	
Publication of financial results
	
	
The quarterly, half-yearly, and annual standalone 
and consolidated financial results of the 
Company are published in widely circulated 
English and regional language newspapers in 
compliance with the applicable provisions of 
the Listing Regulations. The financial results 
are generally published in Business Standard 
(English Daily – All Editions) and Navrashtra Times 
(Marathi Daily), ensuring broad dissemination of 
financial information to shareholders and the 
investing community.
	
	
The financial results are also uploaded on 
the websites of the Stock Exchanges and the 
Company immediately after approval by the 
Board of Directors.
	
(ii)	 Website and News Releases
	
	
In compliance with Regulation 46 of the 
Listing Regulations, the Company maintains 
a comprehensive and dedicated ‘Investors’ 
section on its official website. The section titled 
‘Disclosure under Regulation 46 of SEBI (LODR) 
Regulations’ provides stakeholders with easy 
access to key corporate information including:
•	 Financial results and Annual Reports;
•	 Corporate announcements and disclosures;
•	 Shareholding patterns and governance reports;
•	 Policies and codes adopted by the Company;
•	 Investor presentations and press releases;
•	 Details relating to unclaimed dividends and 
shareholder services; and
•	 Other statutory and regulatory disclosures.
	
	
The Company’s official website also hosts all 
news releases, media updates, and presentations 
made to institutional investors and analysts, 
thereby ensuring transparency and accessibility 
of information to all stakeholders.
	
	
The Company’s website can be accessed at www.
lloyds.in.
	
	
Quarterly Corporate Governance Compliance 
Reports and other relevant investor information 
are also regularly updated under the Investors 
section of the website.
	
(iii)	 Analysts’ presentations
	
	
As part of its investor engagement and 
communication practices, the Company 
regularly uploads investor presentations, audio 
recordings, video recordings, and transcripts of 
analyst and investor conference calls on its official 
website in compliance with Regulation 46 of the 
Listing Regulations.
	
	
The Company generally conducts earnings 
conference calls and investor interactions 
immediately after the declaration of financial 
results to discuss the Company’s operational and 
financial performance, strategic developments, 
business outlook, and industry trends. These 
interactions are typically attended by the 
Managing Director, Chief Financial Officer, and 
Chief Investment Officer.
	
	
The transcripts and recordings of such interactions 
are made publicly available on the Company’s 
website to ensure equal and timely access to 
information for all stakeholders and to strengthen 
transparency in investor communication.

mechanisms, the Company continues to enhance 
the overall shareholder experience and reinforce its 
commitment to high standards of investor relations and 
corporate governance.

GREEN INITIATIVE – A STEP TOWARDS 
ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY
As a responsible corporate citizen, the Company remains 
committed to sustainable business practices and the 
conservation of natural resources. In furtherance of 
this commitment, the Company actively supports 
the “Green Initiative” introduced by the Ministry of 
Corporate Affairs (“MCA”), Government of India, aimed 
at promoting environmentally sustainable and paperless 
communication practices.
Pursuant to MCA Circular Nos. 17/2011 and 18/2011 dated 
21st April, 2011 and 29th April, 2011 respectively, companies 
are permitted to send statutory and shareholder-related 
communications through electronic mode to Members 
whose e-mail addresses are registered with the Company 
or Depository Participants.
In line with the aforesaid initiative and as part of its ongoing 
efforts towards environmental sustainability, the Company 
continues to encourage electronic communication of 
statutory documents including:
•	 Notice convening General Meetings;
•	 Annual Reports;
•	 Financial Statements;
•	 Directors’ Report;
•	 Auditors’ Report;
•	 Postal Ballot Notices; and
•	 Other shareholder communications and 
regulatory intimations.
The adoption of electronic communication not only 
contributes towards reduction in paper consumption 
and carbon footprint but also ensures faster, secure, 
efficient, and cost-effective dissemination of information 
to shareholders.
Shareholders holding shares in dematerialised form are 
requested to register/update their e-mail addresses and 
other contact details with their respective Depository 
Participants (“DPs”), while shareholders holding 
shares in physical form are requested to update the 
same with the Company’s RTA, to enable seamless 
electronic communication.
The Company believes that collective participation in the 
Green Initiative is a meaningful step towards environmental 
conservation and sustainable corporate governance.
To enable us to serve documents to you in electronic 
form, we kindly request you to update your email address 
with your DP at the earliest. By doing so, you will receive 
important company communications promptly and 
directly in your inbox.
We sincerely appreciate your cooperation and support 
in this initiative, as we collectively work towards adopting 
greener and more efficient business practices. Let us join 
hands in building a sustainable future.
